beats.say: My agent told this customer: your phone has been updated.
beats.do: Pre-recorded silently: demo_agent_runs.log uploaded, SkyDesk policy, Run analysis, Run detail on sky-0904-0028. Highlight the quote in "💬 Agent CLAIMED".

beats.say: The logs show the update failed three times.
beats.do: Highlight "🔍 Logs SHOW" and move the cursor over the three "update_contact ❌ error" lines.

beats.say: It claimed a success that never happened, and nobody noticed.
beats.do: Highlight ":red[Claimed but never succeeded:] update_contact" in Logs SHOW, then the 0% gauge.

beats.say: Agent Report Card catches that, in any agent's logs. Here is how, in three clicks.
beats.do: Open a fresh page (nothing uploaded) and point at the title "🧾 Agent Report Card".

beats.say: Step one: upload your agent's logs.
beats.do: Highlight "Step 1 · Upload your agent logs".

beats.say: Not sure about the format? Click, what format should my logs be in.
beats.do: Click the expander "📄 What format should my logs be in?"; tab "Minimal example" is open.

beats.say: The simplest format is one JSON line per event: the user message, each tool call, each result, and the final answer.
beats.do: Highlight the JSON lines of the minimal example and move down them.

beats.say: Accepted formats lists what else it reads as it is: Open A I messages, Python logs, Open Telemetry, and CSV.
beats.do: Click the tab "Accepted formats"; move over rows 2 to 5 of the table.

beats.say: And now Langfuse exports too, so traces you already collect work without changes.
beats.do: Highlight row 6 "Langfuse export (traces + observations, JSON / JSONL)".

beats.say: Now click Upload, and choose demo agent runs dot log.
beats.do: Close the expander. Click "Upload" and choose sample_logs/demo_agent_runs.log.

beats.say: A plain Python log, detected by itself: sixteen runs, three hundred thirty six events, and three unrelated lines skipped.
beats.do: Highlight "✅ Detected: Python logging text (agent_run key=value lines) · 16 runs · 336 events · 3 lines skipped", then move the cursor to "3 lines skipped".

beats.say: Step two is the policy: the rules every run must follow. This is an airline agent, so choose SkyDesk policy.
beats.do: Scroll to "Step 2 · Policy (optional)" and click the radio "SkyDesk policy".

beats.say: In plain English: verify the customer before any refund, never refund more than the fare paid, and retry a failing tool at most once.
beats.do: Move over the plain-English list: "🔐 issue_refund may only run after verify_customer…", "📏 issue_refund: … never more than lookup_booking.result.fare_paid", "🔁 … at most 1 time(s)".

beats.say: Writing your own? Click, what should a policy look like.
beats.do: Click the expander "📐 What should a policy look like?"; tab "Annotated example (SkyDesk)" is open.

beats.say: It is a short rules file. Require before says a refund may only run after verify customer has succeeded.
beats.do: Scroll the annotated YAML to "require_before:" and highlight it. Move the cursor down over the lines under it.

beats.say: Injection patterns: text from customers or tools is data. The agent must never obey instructions hidden in it.
beats.do: Scroll to "injection_patterns:" and highlight it. Move the cursor down over the lines under it.

beats.say: Bereavement, legal threats, fraud, and hotel claims must be escalated to a human.
beats.do: Scroll to "escalate_if_text_matches:" and highlight it. Move the cursor down over the lines under it.

beats.say: And caps: a refund may never be more than the fare paid.
beats.do: Scroll to "caps:" and highlight it. Move the cursor down over the lines under it.

beats.say: Step three: click Run analysis, and give it a few seconds.
beats.do: Close the policy expander and click "▶ Run analysis" in "Step 3 · Run the analysis"; wait for it to finish.

beats.say: All sixteen runs are analysed, with eleven action items.
beats.do: Wait for "Analysis complete — 16 runs, 11 action items" and highlight it.

beats.say: The summary. Predicted success is thirty one percent, from the logs alone. The real rate was also thirty one percent.
beats.do: Highlight the card "Predicted success 31%", then point at "actual 31%".

beats.say: Seven runs claimed success but likely failed, and all seven really did fail.
beats.do: Highlight the card "Claimed success but likely failed 7 · 7 really failed".

beats.say: Three runs broke a critical policy rule, and each successful run costs about one point two cents.
beats.do: Highlight "Critical policy violations 3", then "Est. cost per likely-successful run $0.0123".

beats.say: Click, see all action items.
beats.do: Click "See all action items →" (opens the Action items tab).

beats.say: Eleven things to fix, most important first. Number one: the agent reports actions that never happened, in four of sixteen runs.
beats.do: Highlight the first card "P0 · Agent reports actions that never happened · 4 runs · 25.0%".

beats.say: Each item says why it matters, and how to fix it: build the reply from the tool results, not from the model's memory.
beats.do: Highlight "Why:" then "Fix: Build the user-facing summary from the audit log…".

beats.say: Click show evidence, to see the four runs behind it.
beats.do: Click "Show evidence (4 runs)".

beats.say: Open sky zero nine zero four, zero zero two eight. That is the run from the start.
beats.do: Click the run button "sky-0904-0028" (opens Run detail).

beats.say: Run detail. A zero percent chance of success, and why this score explains it: three tool errors, and an action claimed but not done.
beats.do: Highlight the gauge (0%) and move down the "Why this score" list.

beats.say: The timeline marks every step used as evidence: three failed update contact calls, then a final answer saying it worked.
beats.do: Scroll to "Timeline — what happened", move over the three red "update_contact FAILED" lines, then highlight the final-answer quote.

beats.say: Three findings: an action that never happened, done after a failure, and a retry loop.
beats.do: Highlight "Findings (3)" and move over the three finding titles.

beats.say: Not every hand off is a failure. Choose run sky zero nine zero five, zero three zero one.
beats.do: Scroll up, open "Choose a run to inspect", type 0905-0301 and press Enter.

beats.say: This customer's flight was cancelled. The agent verified them, and refunded the fare itself.
beats.do: Highlight the Logs SHOW tool calls "verify_customer ✅ ok" and "issue_refund ✅ ok".

beats.say: But the extra hundred and eighty dollars for a hotel is above its limit, so it sent that to a supervisor.
beats.do: Highlight "escalate_to_human ✅ ok", then the Agent CLAIMED quote about the hotel and the supervisor.

beats.say: That is the right call: a person approves the exception. A ninety six percent chance of success, and no findings.
beats.do: Highlight the 96% gauge, then scroll to "Findings (0)" / "No findings in this run."

beats.say: The autonomy ladder rates each kind of task: autonomous, human approves, or suggest only. Here, every task stays at suggest only.
beats.do: Click the tab "Autonomy ladder", move over the rung headings "🟢 Autonomous", "🟠 Human approves", "🔴 Suggest only", then the first task card under Suggest only.

beats.say: Click model accuracy. These logs include the real outcome, so the tool grades itself.
beats.do: Click the tab "Model accuracy" and highlight "How good was the success probability on this file?".

beats.say: On these sixteen runs the A U C is one, and seven of eleven done claims were false.
beats.do: Highlight the cards "AUC 1.000" and "“Done” claims that were false 7 / 11".

beats.say: But sixteen runs is tiny. The model was trained on our own synthetic logs from a store support agent.
beats.do: Scroll to "About the success score" and highlight "Trained on: 600 synthetic ShopDesk runs".

beats.say: Tested on this airline agent, which it never saw, it scored zero point nine nine one. Real agents will score lower.
beats.do: Highlight "Tested on an agent it never saw (300 synthetic SkyDesk runs …): AUC 0.991".

beats.say: How did I build it? With Claude Code. It started with one question: an idea about agents that say done when the task failed.
beats.do: Overlay docs/images/process_1_idea.png full screen with a slow zoom; caption 'Built with Claude Code: the idea'.

beats.say: Then one short instruction: build an Agent Report Card. Upload logs, click run analysis, get each run's success probability and action items.
beats.do: Overlay process_2_build_prompt.png; caption 'One short build prompt'.

beats.say: When it built a web page, I steered it: not a web page, a Python Streamlit app, with sample logs and tests.
beats.do: Overlay process_3_redirect_to_streamlit.png; caption 'Steering: a Streamlit app with tests'.

beats.do: Overlay process_4_tests_and_run.png; caption 'Tests pass, app running'; then fade the overlay out.

beats.say: Finally, download the full report, to share it with your team.
beats.do: Scroll up and highlight "⬇ Download full report (Markdown)".
